claims.reason_summary: For D>0, the state map is bijective and V†V=I. Sector dephasing sends the signal probabilities through T. The noise contribution is identical across outcomes and is preserved by T because its rows sum to one. Thus p_dephased=T p_native, including smoothing.

At ε=0 with an invertible frame, each effect has rank at most one, so its norm equals its trace and both routes have R=d−1. With smoothing, the stated interval follows from ||f_i||²≤||F_i||op≤tr(F_i). Its width bounds the absolute route difference by Nε tr(D⁻¹), at most Ndε/(m+Nε) when M≥mI.

The supplied implementation uses ||H||op=√7/4, giving normalized edges (r,s) with r²+s²=1 and hence θ=τ. The middle-outcome difference (plus minus minus) is 2(v₀s−v₁r)sin(τ)cos(τ)/(3/2+9ε)=−√(3/7)sin(τ)cos(τ)/(3/2+9ε). It is nonzero at τ=1/4 despite identical native distributions, ruling out fixed classical post-processing.
